findings.title: CaSKG currently has a paper-to-repository replay-readiness mismatch
findings.observation: The current CaSKG paper links an official GitHub repository as code availability, but the inspected official repository ZhiyuanLi218/Caskg currently contains only README.md. That README says the code will be released within a few days. Therefore the paper's current code-availability link is not yet a replayable static evidence package at this observation time.
findings.scope_guard: This is a time-scoped observation of the current official repository, not a claim that code or artifacts will never be released. Git timestamps are chronology metadata only.

findings.title: CaSKG specifies a promising per-episode evidence contract but does not currently expose the bytes needed for Chat-only verification
findings.observation: The paper states that accepted evaluation records contain per-episode outcomes, environment steps, retrieved context and infrastructure diagnostics, while evaluation fixes the task cohort, prompt, evaluator, episode limits and environment interaction loop. This is close to a useful replay/evidence contract. However, the current official repository exposes none of the claimed per-episode records, candidate graph/frontier, counterfactual-probe scores, published graph, or run manifests, so the table results cannot currently be recomputed from public static artifacts in scheduled Chat.
findings.scope_guard: The absence claim is limited to the inspected official repository and exact public artifact searches in this run.

findings.title: CaSKG counterfactual edge probing is a text-level LLM proxy, not an environment intervention
findings.observation: CaSKG's counterfactual edge-probing stage asks an LLM to assess removal, substitution and reordering of textual skill descriptions and returns support scores. This is a useful structural-calibration mechanism, but it is not the same evidence class as actually replaying the environment under an edge intervention. The downstream component ablations are system-level performance evidence and should not be promoted to edge-level causal treatment effects.
findings.scope_guard: This distinguishes mechanism/evidence classes; it does not dispute the reported aggregate performance differences.

findings.title: CaSKG's paper itself exposes heterogeneous provenance classes
findings.observation: The paper distinguishes richer per-episode accepted records from some scale-study values described as archived aggregate records, and notes aggregate counterparts where episode directories are not available. Aggregate table values therefore cannot automatically be treated as equivalent to a per-episode replay archive with retrieved-context and infrastructure diagnostics.
findings.scope_guard: Do not infer that aggregate records are invalid; they simply support a weaker replay/provenance claim than full per-episode records.

protocol_status.preflight: 15/15 Draft-2020-12 structurally valid; 15/15 expected semantic decisions matched
protocol_status.reason: Existing evaluated-run source binding, replay export/coverage, claim-output semantic binding and paired-randomness gates already fail closed on the observed CaSKG package gaps and proxy-vs-executed-intervention distinction.

phase1_assessment.accepted_scope: The static paper/repository audit is Chat-native and quota-independent. CaSKG itself is not yet an accepted replay route because the public executable/evidence package is not currently present.

termination_cause: runtime checkpoint; research frontier remains open

If code/artifacts landed, inspect whether candidate graph/frontier, text-level counterfactual probe scores, published graph, per-episode accepted records, retrieved-context fields, infrastructure diagnostics, source/model/provider revisions and evaluation manifests are public and immutable enough for zero-cost static replay auditing.
